scope_statement.text: Covers detailing of in-situ corbels, beam half joints and continuous nibs. Closely related to joint design; designer must ensure detail design is clearly specified. Does not cover all aspects of precast corbels/half joints/nibs. Bearing pad design is out of scope.

member_types.name: Corbel
member_types.description: Short cantilever projection from a column/wall face used to support a bearing load (e.g. a beam end).

member_types.name: Half joint (beam)
member_types.description: A stepped/notched end of a beam that provides a reduced-depth bearing seat for a supported member.

member_types.name: Continuous nib
member_types.description: A linear (continuous, not discrete) projection along a beam or wall used as a bearing seat, e.g. for slabs or brickwork support.
model_details: MN2 (horizontal U-bars — shallow nib for light loads, e.g. brickwork)

zones_terminology: column links (top of column, near corbel)
supporting beam (for nibs — the vertical link leg in the supporting beam carries the nib reaction)

connections_to_other_members.corbel: Column (corbel cantilevers from column; two column links placed close to corbel top per MCB1/MCB2)
connections_to_other_members.half_joint: Beam-to-beam or beam-to-slab bearing (MN1 detail 'also suitable for half joints in slabs')
connections_to_other_members.nib: Beam or wall (nib is on a beam/wall; supported member — e.g. slab or brickwork — bears on nib); vertical link leg of the SUPPORTING beam carries the nib's load

corbels.dependency_note: See 5.2.1 (general chapter, not in this extract) for values of Δcdev.

corbels.fire_note: For 4-hour fire resistance, supplementary reinforcement may be required where nominal cover exceeds 40mm (axis distance to main reinforcement exceeds 70mm) — EC2 Part 1.2 Cl.4.5.2.

generic_model_detail_notes.nibs_MN2: Nominal cover specified by designer (normally to ensure 40mm to the main steel).

MCB1_specific_dimensions.column_links: Two column links placed close to corbel top.

edge_distance_to_bearing.text: Distance between edge of bearing and outside of plate or bar should not be less than the vertical cover to the plate or bar.

MCB2_specific_dimensions.column_links: Two column links placed close to corbel top.
MCB2_specific_dimensions.welding_note: Main tensile bars welded to a cross bar or plate, and to the vertical compression bars.

edge_distance_to_bearing.text: Distance between edge of bearing and inside of bar to be a minimum of the bar diameter or 0.75 × cover, whichever is greater.

MHJ_specific_dimensions.horizontal_U_bar_diameter: Same diameter as main bottom bars.
MHJ_specific_dimensions.bearing_pad_note: Special design information must be given concerning the bearing pads.

edge_distance.text: Not less than bar diameter or 0.75 × nominal cover, whichever is greater.

min_nominal_overlap_of_reinforcement_mm.meaning: Minimum nominal overlap of reinforcement in nib and reinforcement in supported member.

MN1_specific_dimensions.reinforcement_options: Closed links or U-bars may be used.

MN2_specific_dimensions.wiring_requirement: Lacer bar wired to at least two main longitudinal bars.
MN2_specific_dimensions.suitability: Shallow nibs suitable for light loads (e.g. supporting brickwork).

reinforcement_types.name: Main tensile reinforcement (corbel)
reinforcement_types.location: Top of corbel, extended as close to outer face as possible
reinforcement_types.extension_rule: Must extend beyond the load-bearing area by at least the minimum distance shown on the Model Details.
reinforcement_types.anchorage: Tension lap at column face (into column); large radius bend required where reinforcement changes direction
reinforcement_types.preferred_form: Small bar diameters, horizontal U-bars, or links with easy bends (preferred). Large diameters (requiring welding, MCB2) only where loading is high and geometry restrictive.
reinforcement_types.notes: It is essential the main tensile reinforcement is extended as close to the outer face of the corbel as possible.

reinforcement_types.name: Compression bars (corbel)
reinforcement_types.location: Bottom of corbel / column compression zone
reinforcement_types.area_requirement: Total area ≥ 1000 mm²/metre width of corbel (both MCB1 and MCB2)
reinforcement_types.geometry_note: Outer compression bars angled to pass inside links (MCB1).

reinforcement_types.name: Secondary horizontal reinforcement / horizontal links (corbel)
reinforcement_types.purpose: Crack control / shear resistance in corbel body
reinforcement_types.area_requirement: Total area not less than 0.50 × area of main tensile reinforcement

reinforcement_types.name: Column links (at corbel)
reinforcement_types.location: Placed close to corbel top, within the column

reinforcement_types.name: Nominal H8 'U' bar (staircase fragment, MST2)
reinforcement_types.note: Position of H8 U-bar specified separately from design reinforcement; adjustable bends on site.

reinforcement_types.name: Horizontal 'U' bar (half joint / nib)
reinforcement_types.diameter_rule_MHJ: Same diameter as main bottom bars
reinforcement_types.purpose: Tension anchorage at nib/half-joint root; standard radius of bend

reinforcement_types.name: Full-length links (half joint)
reinforcement_types.purpose: Sufficient to resist total reaction, equally spaced

reinforcement_types.name: Closed links / U-bars (nib, MN1)
reinforcement_types.purpose: Take load on nib; specified by designer
reinforcement_types.constraint: Diameter of links not more than 12mm

reinforcement_types.name: Lacer bar (nib, MN2)
reinforcement_types.function: Ties/restrains the horizontal U-bars; wired to at least two main longitudinal bars

corbel_MCB1_MCB2.tension_lap: Shown at the main tensile reinforcement / column interface (labelled 'Tension lap' on both details).
corbel_MCB1_MCB2.compression_anchorage: Shown separately from the tension lap, at the compression bars.

half_joint_MHJ.tension_lap_for_cranked_bar: Separate, distinct lap noted specifically for the cranked bar.

nib_MN1.description: Minimum nominal overlap of reinforcement in nib and reinforcement in supported member.

laps.general_table: Table 6.12 gives typical full tension/compression lap lengths (l0) in bar diameters for good/poor bond conditions across four fck/fcu grades — see formulas_and_calculations.

table_6_12_assumptions: α1, α2, α4, α5 of EC2 Table 8.2 all = 1
α6 = 1.5 (assumes more than 50% of bars lapped at one place) — for laps only
For other situations, refer to EC2 Clause 8.4.4
anchorage_and_development.corbel_specific: Main tensile reinforcement anchored via tension lap into the column; large radius of bend required at the anchorage/direction-change point (both MCB1 and MCB2).
anchorage_and_development.half_joint_specific: Tension anchorage shown for the horizontal U-bar and for straight/cranked main bars; hh (bar diameter-derived?) dimension labelled at anchorage in MHJ diagram (value not given numerically in source, symbol only).

nib_specific.MN1: Tension anchorage length required if U-bars are used.
nib_specific.MN2: Tension anchorage length shown for horizontal U-bars; depth of nib not less than 140mm partly to accommodate this.

anchorage_and_development.dependency: DEPENDENCY: General anchorage/development-length numerical rules and bend-radius/hook rules should be taken from the General Detailing chapter and EC2 Cl.8.4/8.7, not invented here.

spacing.condition: General corbel/half-joint/nib reinforcement, poker-vibrator access required

spacing.rule: Minimum vertical space 25mm or bar size, whichever greater

spacing.condition: Continuous nib, main bars, general area
Continuous nib, main bars, concentrated load area
Continuous nib, secondary bars, general area
Continuous nib, secondary bars, concentrated load area

bar_curtailment.note: Source does not give explicit curtailment-length rules for corbels/half joints/nibs beyond anchorage-length and lap requirements above; curtailment as such (mid-span bar cutoffs) is not applicable to these short, statically-determinate cantilever/bearing elements in the way it is for beams/slabs.
bar_curtailment.fact_type: INFORMATION GAP — no explicit curtailment content in source for this topic

large_radius_bends.requirement: Large radius of bend required at main tensile reinforcement direction changes in corbels (MCB1, MCB2) to avoid crushing the concrete / for crack control.
applies_to: MCB2 main tensile bars welded to cross bar/plate

U_bars.MHJ: Horizontal U-bar, same diameter as main bottom bars, standard radius of bend.
U_bars.MN1: U-bars optional alternative to closed links.
U_bars.MN2: Horizontal U-bars, diameter not more than 16mm.

cranked_bars.MHJ: Cranked bars used if necessary for crack control; have their own distinct tension lap.

bar_bending.welding_as_bend_alternative: Where large bar diameters are needed (>16mm typically), welding main tensile bars to a cross bar or plate (MCB2) is used instead of/alongside bending, because large-diameter bends become impractical; welding normally done off-site under factory conditions.

corbel: outer face zone (main tensile bar termination)
column-interface zone (tension lap, compression anchorage, two column links)
body zone (secondary horizontal reinforcement/links, compression bars)
half_joint: bearing/nib root zone (tension anchorage, hanger links at 450, cranked-bar lap)
full length zone (full-length links resisting total reaction, equally spaced)
continuous_nib: root/anchorage zone (tension anchorage length for U-bars)
concentrated-load zone (tighter max bar pitch, 2h≤250 vs 3h≤400)
general span zone (normal max pitch rules)

corbel_to_column.reinforcement_interaction: Corbel main tensile reinforcement lapped in tension into column reinforcement at the corbel/column interface; two additional column links placed close to corbel top; compression bars given compression anchorage into column.

nib_to_supporting_beam.reinforcement_interaction: The vertical leg of the links in the supporting beam must be designed to carry the loads from the nib; effective depth d of the beam should be reduced because concrete in the nib below the vertical beam link does not contribute to resistance.

nib_to_supported_member.reinforcement_interaction: Minimum nominal overlap of 60mm between reinforcement in the nib and reinforcement in the supported member (MN1).

detailing_sequence_implied: 1. Establish concrete grade (≥28/35) and member geometry (corbel projection / half-joint step / nib depth, min 140mm for shallow nib MN2).
2. Establish nominal cover (internal/external, corbel vs. nib/half-joint values) per exposure class.
3. Check minimum reinforcement area (tension As,min, compression Asc,min for corbels; As,min for half joints/nibs).
4. Select main tensile reinforcement arrangement: small-diameter bars/U-bars/easy-bend links preferred; large diameter + welding (MCB2) only if loading/geometry demands.
5. Provide compression bars/anchorage and secondary horizontal reinforcement/links (≥0.5× main tensile area).
6. Place two column links close to corbel top (corbel case).
7. Check bar spacing (min pitch 75mm; min vertical spacing 25mm/bar size; nib max pitch rules by zone).
8. Check anchorage (min 10⌀ or 100mm; Table 6.12 for specific lengths) and laps (tension lap at column/support interface; 60mm min overlap for nibs).
9. Confirm edge distances to bearing (bar diameter or 0.75×cover, whichever greater).

member_definition.scope: Covers design/detailing principles for prestressed concrete elements commonly used in buildings: flat slabs, banded beams, trough/waffle slabs, transfer structures. Principles also apply to bridges (not detailed here).

methods.name: Pre-tensioning
methods.description: Reinforcement stressed between steel buttresses before casting; concrete cast around the stressed tendons. Typically factory-cast precast units delivered to site.

methods.name: Post-tensioning
methods.description: Steel stressed in a duct installed in concrete after the concrete reaches specified strength. Used for in-situ concrete frames; the main focus of this section.

items: Setting-out data per tendon: profile and tolerances (vertical & horizontal)
Forces to be applied per tendon and tensioning sequence
Location of grouting points and vents
Connection detail consideration with shear walls/bracing points
Debonded tendons marked on sections/elevations with method and length of debonding
Tendon deflection dimensioned horizontally and vertically (radius of curvature per manufacturer)
Concrete grade and minimum strength at transfer of prestress

Design parameters: relaxation of prestressing steel, duct friction/wobble factors, anchorage draw-in, modulus of elasticity/tendon extension, movement of permanent structure at stressing, camber variation
Method of marking tendons on slab soffit
notes: Choice of prestressing system left to specialist contractor when not shown on drawings, or where alternative system is permitted — must be stated.
Original Detailer/Designer should check any contractor-proposed alternative, especially reinforcement modifications.
Where clashes occur between tendons and reinforcement (links/main steel), inserts, or pipes — tendons take priority (must be stated on drawings).
Calcium chloride (harmful additive, corrosive to tendons) must not be used — must be stated.

min_clear_spacing_pretensioned_tendons.note: φ = tendon diameter, dg = max aggregate size; multiple governing minima per Figure 7.4 (values partially OCR-garbled — see information gaps).

geometry_pretensioned.centroid_rule: For symmetrical concrete sections, centroid of tendons should lie on the vertical centroidal axis (Fig. 7.3).

min_clear_spacing_posttensioned_ducts.note: φ = duct diameter, dg = max aggregate size (Fig. 7.5; values OCR-garbled — treat with caution).

geometry_posttensioned_ducts.coupler_location_rule: Couplers located away from intermediate supports; avoid placing couplers on ≥50% of tendons at one cross-section.
geometry_posttensioned_ducts.tendon_deviation_without_deviator: Up to 0.01 radians permitted without a deviator.

cmin_b_posttensioned_ducts.rectangular: greater of smaller dimension or half the greater dimension
cmin_b_posttensioned_ducts.cap: No requirement for more than 80mm for either duct shape.

nominal_cover_prestressing.durability_cover: cmin,dur + Δcdev as for reinforced concrete (slabs 6.2 / beams 6.3 — not in this extract; dependency).

reinforcement_types.name: Bursting reinforcement (end block)
reinforcement_types.purpose: Resist tensile bursting forces behind anchorages, acting in all lateral planes.
reinforcement_types.detailing_requirement: Full tensile laps; large radius bends to avoid crushing concrete.
reinforcement_types.positioning: As near as possible to outer edge of largest similar/concentric prism to the anchor plate; at least 50mm outside edge of anchor plate.

reinforcement_types.name: Face-zone reinforcement (spalling control)
reinforcement_types.purpose: Resist tensile stresses on end-block faces adjacent to anchorages, prevent spalling.
reinforcement_types.placement: Two directions at right angles, as close to end face as cover permits.

reinforcement_types.name: Un-tensioned reinforcement at column positions (flat slabs)
reinforcement_types.placement: Concentrated between lines 1.5×slab depth either side of column width; near top of floor.
reinforcement_types.extension: At least anchorage length beyond 0.2×L into span, or as needed by calculation.

reinforcement_types.name: Un-tensioned bottom reinforcement (flat slabs, span zone, unbonded tendons)
reinforcement_types.condition: Required when unbonded tendons used in span zone.
reinforcement_types.extension: At least to within 0.2×L (plus anchorage length) from centre of support.

reinforcement_types.name: Shear reinforcement (post-tensioned beams)
reinforcement_types.form: Open links or pairs of lapping U-bars (to allow tendon positioning around them).

reinforcement_types.name: Anti-spalling reinforcement
reinforcement_types.condition: Fire ratings > 2 hours, when no other reinforcement provided in soffit.

reinforcement_types.name: Trimmer bars (stressing pockets)
reinforcement_types.note: Require proper anchorage; total area of longitudinal bars to equal area of prestressing steel being anchored at pocket.

reinforcement_types.name: Reinforcement in unstressed slab zones
reinforcement_types.area: Greater of 0.13%·b·h, or 1/4 of reinforcement parallel to edge.
reinforcement_types.extension: Greater of la or 0.7·la, plus full anchorage length into slab.

reinforcement_types.name: Reinforcement at end zone of pre-tensioned beam (transmission length)
reinforcement_types.form: Standard stirrups, closer spacing (e.g. 75mm) in transmission zone.

laps.end_block_links: Reinforcement links for adjacent anchorages should be overlapped; longitudinal bars positioned in corners.
laps.general_note: Bursting reinforcement (hoops/spirals) must be detailed with full tensile laps.

anchorage_and_development.corner_bars_end_block: At all corners, bars should have large radius bends to avoid crushing concrete, or pass round a longitudinal bar/tendon of at least the same diameter.
anchorage_and_development.un_tensioned_flat_slab_reinf: Extends beyond 0.2×L an anchorage length (see above).

spacing.condition: Un-tensioned top reinforcement at flat-slab columns
Un-tensioned bottom reinforcement, span zone, unbonded tendons

formulas.name: bursting_force_ratio
formulas.formula: Fbst/Po per Table 7.3, keyed by ypo/yo

formulas.name: grouting_pressure
formulas.value: 0.1 MPa typical for slabs and beams

drawing_conventions_specific.tendon_legend_symbols: Symbols for 1–5+ tendons per group (dot patterns), live end, dead end, intermediate anchor/stressing anchor, weave, 'add tendons', placing sequence numbers, colour code, tendon stressing reference numbers (Figs 7.29–7.30).
drawing_conventions_specific.duct_profile_tabulation: Duct profile given in tabular form (x, y, z coordinates per Fig 7.9), profiles tabulated separately per vertical row of ducts, referenced to an on-site datum; dimensions to top or bottom of duct, frequent enough to define the curvature.
drawing_conventions_specific.soffit_marking: Soffit of slabs should be marked to show tendon positions (for future reference / to avoid drilling into tendons).

notes_and_callouts: Choice of prestressing system left to specialist contractor where not shown / alternative permitted — statement required on drawing.
Tendons take priority over reinforcement/inserts/pipes at clashes — statement required on drawing.
Calcium chloride must not be used — statement required on drawing.
Drilling/demolition: specify specialist drilling techniques to avoid hitting tendons; specify safe demolition sequence per CDM, particularly for unbonded tendons (sudden energy release risk).

material_information.concrete_grade_generic: Not fixed generically in this section (project/design specific); grade referenced elsewhere (e.g. transfer strength, minimum start grade for corbels/nibs is 28/35 from §6.9).

member_definition.scope: General practice notes for detailing precast concrete work — transport, handling, joints, tolerances. Not member-specific geometry.

key_practice_notes: Precast unit transported after manufacture, before incorporation — tolerances matter when built into part-built/ready-built structures.
Unit often made by third party without site visit/full drawings — clarity of instruction vital.
Special consideration of joints required; sound detailing of joints leads to attractive/serviceable/safe structures.
Casting orientation decision often best left to/discussed with precaster.
Avoid acute re-entrant corners (formwork removal damage) and acute protruding corners (handling breakage, poor aggregate compaction/discoloration).

transport_limits_UK.economic_note: Most frequent load: 20 tonne payload on 32 tonne gross truck; savings if total unit weight per load approaches (without exceeding) 30 tonne, e.g. 2×9.8t vs 1×10.2t.

lifting_and_handling: Permissible support points and packing materials should be noted on drawing.
Lifting strengths for concrete stated on drawing (minimum lifting strength specified for mould-reuse economy).
Unit weight for craneage/transportation stated on drawing.
Reinforcement generally NOT suitable for use as lifting hooks (though some manufacturers do, with care/testing).
Proprietary lifting/fixing inserts used per manufacturer instructions with adequate safety factors; isolate fixings from secondary load effects/structural movements not designed for.
Where a drawing shows part of a unit cast onto another precast unit, clearly state which weights apply to which part.

joints.reference: Design of joints & reinforcement/concrete requirements (binding links, chamfers) covered in IStructE report 'Structural joints in precast concrete', 1978.
joints.in_situ_to_precast_interface: Precast units should have a key joint cast into the mutual face for mechanical anchorage/shear where in-situ concrete is placed adjacent (e.g. infill slab); precast face receiving in-situ concrete should be properly prepared (e.g. scabbled while 'green').

durability_special_case.context: Bridge/car park construction with chloride exposure risk (XD3) — joints between precast units require special corrosion protection attention.
durability_special_case.figure_ref: Figure 8.1 shows moderate/severe/very-severe exposure zones for precast car parks and bridges (splash zone, soffit/beam ends behind sealant, transverse beams/floor slab).

member_definition.scope: Detailing generally follows normal RC structures except reinforcement provision/spacing, cover, and durability requirements are more onerous. Governed by BS EN 1992-3 (EC2 Part 3).
member_definition.key_difference_from_normal_structures: Serviceability (crack width) often controls design/reinforcement quantity, not just ultimate strength. Construction and movement joints MUST be shown on drawings (not just specification) because reinforcement for thermal/shrinkage restraint depends on joint frequency/spacing — Designer's responsibility to position all joints.

table_9_1.requirement: Some leakage acceptable / leakage of liquids irrelevant.
Leakage limited to small amount; some surface staining/damp patches acceptable.
Leakage minimal; appearance not impaired by staining.

tightness_classes.class_0_detail: Same provisions as retaining walls apply. Minimum wall thickness 120mm.

class_1_detail.crack_width_formula: wk1: for hD/hw ≤ 5, wk1=0.2mm; for hD/hw ≥ 25, wk1=0.05mm; linear interpolation between.
class_1_detail.rationale: Limiting crack width to these values should allow effective self-healing within a relatively short time.

class_2_detail.note: Cracks passing through full section thickness should generally be avoided unless liners/water bars incorporated.

tightness_classes.class_3_detail: Special measures (liners or prestress) generally required.
tightness_classes.aesthetic_case: Where aesthetic appearance critical, crack width limited to 0.1mm.

cover.note: Greater cover may be needed at faces in contact with aggressive soils, or subject to erosion/abrasion.

spacing.rule: Pitch reduces rapidly — see EC2 Part 3 Cl.7.3.3 (dependency, not fully restated here)

prestressed_walls.min_passive_reinforcement: 300 mm²/m or 0.001·Ac, each direction, each face.

circular_tanks.tendon_centroid_rule: Should generally lie in outer third of wall thickness; may relax to outer half if cover otherwise impossible.

opening_corners.rule: Detailing must ensure diagonal tension faces adequately catered for; strut-and-tie system (EC2 Cl.5.6.4) is an appropriate design approach.
